bonds.analysis: For a balanced portfolio, I recommend a diversified mix of investment-grade bonds from developed markets, following a laddered maturity structure to minimize interest rate risk. The maturity buckets will be allocated as follows: 30% of the portfolio in 2-year bonds, 20% in 5-year bonds, 20% in 7-year bonds, and 30% in a combination of shorter and longer-term bonds to ensure that no more than 30% of the portfolio mature in any single year, according to the laddered structure. We will hold our existing AA+ rated 5-year bond in the developed region at an allocation of 0.25. This recommendation maintains a portfolio duration below 10 years and avoids emerging market sovereign or corporate debt. It also adheres to the required credit rating and laddered maturity structure constraints. A laddered structure like this helps to lock in returns today while offering the potential for higher yields on longer-term bonds. I suggest rebalancing the portfolio quarterly to maintain the desired allocation.

The remaining 90% of the portfolio will be allocated across the other asset classes.
